body.html:
A mind-blowing incident from Lakhimpur Kheri, UP has left everyone stunned! 😱 A terrified husband actually got his own wife married to her lover in front of the entire village panchayat!

💔 The story: 42-year-old farmer Gurnam Singh discovered his wife Rajwinder Kaur's affair with their neighbor. But instead of confronting them, fear took over - he was so scared his wife might harm him that he called the panchayat himself!

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 The couple has 3 children together, but Gurnam literally said "take her away, leave my life" and handed her over to her lover!

🎥 The viral video shows the woman and her lover standing together as he promises to take care of her and the three children. The entire village witnessed this unprecedented "love marriage" arranged by the husband himself!

🤔 But plot twist - now even the lover is reportedly having second thoughts about the woman!

📱 Social media is buzzing with one question: "Does this even happen?!"
Local authorities are investigating this unique case of love, fear, and panchayat justice that has shocked the entire district!

articles.title: Man in Burqa Assaulted in Shamli; Police Deny Temple Entry Claims
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a disturbing incident from Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, a man named Sunil from Haryana was caught roaming in the city on May 23, 2025, while wearing a burqa. Locals, suspicious of his behavior, confronted him, only to discover that he was a man.

body.html:
In a disturbing incident from Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, a man named Sunil from Haryana was caught roaming in the city on May 23, 2025, while wearing a burqa. Locals, suspicious of his behavior, confronted him, only to discover that he was a man. A video of the incident shows Sunil being assaulted by a group of people.

According to Sunil's family, he is mentally unstable. The police have registered an FIR against those involved in the assault.

Meanwhile, claims circulating on social media allege that Sunil had entered a temple wearing the burqa. However, Shamli police have refuted these claims, stating there was no evidence of him entering any temple.

articles.title: Kanpur: Retired Engineer’s Nose Bitten Off in Shocking Parking Dispute
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a gruesome incident in Kanpur, a parking dispute at Ratan Planet Apartment in the Bithoor police station area turned violent when a flat owner allegedly bit off the nose of a retired engineer.

body.html:
In a gruesome incident in Kanpur, a parking dispute at Ratan Planet Apartment in the Bithoor police station area turned violent when a flat owner allegedly bit off the nose of a retired engineer.

According to reports, the dispute erupted between the apartment's society secretary and the flat owner, Kshitij, after he saw a car parked in his designated space. An argument broke out, during which Kshitij allegedly slapped the retired engineer and then bit his nose in a shocking act of aggression.

The entire incident was caught on the apartment’s CCTV camera.

Kanpur Police confirmed that a case has been registered at the Bithoor police station under relevant sections of the IPC, and an investigation is currently underway.

articles.title: PM Modi: Indus Water Treaty Hampered Dam Maintenance, India Begins Desilting Operations
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has raised concerns over the limitations imposed by the 1960 Indus Water Treaty, stating that it prevented India from undertaking desilting operations in its dams, which in turn reduced their capacity over time.

body.html:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has raised concerns over the limitations imposed by the 1960 Indus Water Treaty, stating that it prevented India from undertaking desilting operations in its dams, which in turn reduced their capacity over time.

"The Indus Water Treaty of 1960 prevented India from the desilting of the dams. This reduced the capacity of the dams. Doesn't India have the right to its waters? The treaty is in abeyance now... the cleaning of dams has started," PM Modi said.

His remarks come amid growing debates around the future of the treaty and India’s water rights, especially in the context of increasing tensions and the need for improved water management infrastructure.
